model_args.text: Can a virus modify human DNA? Viruses are simple organisms that do not have the ability to replicate without the help of host cells. Once a virus infects a human cell, its genetic material can integrate into human DNA, but this does not mean that it is directly modifying human DNA. When a virus integrates its genetic material into human DNA, it is called a provirus. The provirus remains inactive in human DNA and does not cause any damage or changes to human genetic material. However, in some rare cases, a virus can integrate into the wrong place in human DNA and cause a genetic mutation. But this is extremely rare and is not a common form of viral infection. In summary, although viruses can integrate their genetic material into human DNA, it is not common for them to directly modify human DNA. Viruses are more likely to cause disease and damage to host cells in other ways, such as by replicating inside them and killing them or causing inflammation.
